entry.body: Improving Alcaraz underlines title credentials in wide-open draw - Published Carlos Alcaraz swept Wu Yibing aside to reach the US Open fourth round - and said he is getting better with every match as he continues his return from a long-term injury lay-off. The Spaniard underlined why he remains a serious contender to defend his title in New York with a 6-3 6-4 6-1 victory over China's Wu. The 23-year-old's opening-round match in Flushing Meadows was his first on a singles court for 139 days after injuring his wrist in April. Alcaraz came through his opener in straight sets but had to battle back from a set down against Portugal's Jaime Faria in the second round. However, Alcaraz continued to build momentum on Friday, needing two hours and 20 minutes on court to beat Wu. "To be honest, I'm better than I thought," the seven-time major champion said. "Physically I thought I was going to be bad after the first match, but I am recovering really well. I am doing great things off the court to be in a good state. "Right now, I think my level is really good. I think I have caught the rhythm of the competition. "Every time that I step on the court I give it all. I'm just trying to improve, be better every match and I think I'm getting there." American 20th seed Tommy Paul - who Alcaraz has beaten six times in a row - awaits in the fourth round. Alcaraz's path to an eighth major title has opened up over the past few days. French Open champion and Wimbledon runner-up Alexander Zverev heads the men's draw in the absence of injured world number one Jannik Sinner. As the second seed, Alcaraz cannot meet Zverev until the final - and the German has been taken to five sets and kept on court until 2am in his two matches so far. Novak Djokovic suffered a shock first-round exit to Argentine Mariano Navone, while Canadian third seed Felix Auger-Aliassime lost to Karen Khachanov in the second round. As it stands, American eighth seed Ben Shelton is the only top-10 player that Alcaraz can meet before the semi-finals. He could then face seventh seed Daniil Medvedev in the last four. Alcaraz has won all three of his meetings with Shelton and has a 6-3 winning head-to-head against Medvedev - although the inconsistent Russian beat him at Indian Wells in March. Meanwhile, Zverev's potential pre-final opponents include home hope Taylor Fritz and Italy's French Open runner-up Flavio Cobolli. - 'It's so strong' - Sabalenka halts play over cannabis smell - Published4 hours ago - 100 influencers invited to US Open spark debate on 'tennis etiquette' - Published19 hours ago 'Alcaraz more of a favourite with each win' While Alcaraz at times appeared frustrated with his own inconsistency against Wu, the former world number three continues to demonstrate progress. Alcaraz landed 21 winners as he extended his career-best streak of Grand Slam singles match wins to 17, but that was counteracted by 33 unforced errors and a first-serve success rate of just 67%. Despite a seemingly straightforward scoreline, Alcaraz did not have it all his own way and repeatedly made his feelings clear on the court. He surrendered early advantages in the first two sets - his first serve dipped to 53% in the second set - but managed to reset to avoid further complications. "Every win Alcaraz gets, he is becoming more of a favourite," former Wimbledon champion Pat Cash said on BBC Radio 5 Live. "Four months off, no matches and win the US Open? He is a class above everybody else, when he is good, and he is getting better by the moment. "The way he is moving, there is no reason for him not to do well." Former champion Medvedev also progressed on Friday, overcoming French 26th seed Arthur Rinderknech 6-4 6-4 6-4. Medvedev achieved his sole major title at the US Open in 2021, and has won 21 of his 23 singles titles on hard courts. He appears in the form to challenge again, on the evidence of his three straight-set victories so far, but will have to overcome American 11th seed Frances Tiafoe or Monaco's 22nd seed Valentin Vacherot next. Britons Henry Patten and Joe Salisbury both won their men's doubles first-round matches. Top seeds Patten and Finnish parner Harri Heliovaara won 6-4 6-2 against Argentine brothers Francisco and Juan Manuel Cerundolo, while Salisbury and American Rajeev Ram beat Australian John-Patrick Smith and Mexico's Santiago Gonzalez 7-6 (7-3) 7-6 (8-6). Jan Choinski and Bulgaria's Alexander Donski also advanced with a 7-6 (7-5) 6-4 win over American pair Martin Damm and Mackenzie McDonald. Related topics - Published28 August

entry.title: Greaves becomes first woman to win match on European Tour
entry.body: Greaves becomes first woman to win match on European Tour - Published Beau Greaves made darts history by becoming the first woman to win a match on the European Tour. The 22-year-old, who was edged out 6-5 by Rob Cross on her European Tour debut in Hungary last week, beat Daryl Gurney 6-4 in the Czech Open. Gurney beat Greaves in a deciding set in their first-round match at the PDC World Championship in December and he moved into a 3-1 lead in Prague. However, Greaves reeled off three straight legs with 14, 13 and 11-dart finishes to go 4-3 in front and, even though Gurney levelled at 4-4, she went on to take victory and become the first female winner in the European Tour's 15-year history. "It feels amazing," said Greaves, who will play world number two Luke Humphries in the second round on Saturday. "It's just so nice to win a game, I was so nervous at the start, I don't know why. It took me so long to get settled, but luckily I did enough to win the game. "It means loads to me, the crowd's fantastic. It's such a tight stage and you feel so much from the crowd. I'm really enjoying it and loving the experience." It is the latest in a list of achievements for Doncaster's Greaves which include her becoming the first woman to win a PDC ranking title when she beat Michael Smith in April. She is also the first woman to hit a nine-dart finish on the PDC ProTour, having done so in a win against Mensur Suljovic in February. Greaves also won the Women's World Matchplay for the third time when she beat Fallon Sherrock in July. On facing Humphries, she added: "I've played Luke on the big stage before so I know what to expect, he's world class so I'm going to have to play a lot better than I did tonight. "What more do you want than on a Euro Tour to play one of the best players in the world? I'll look forward to it and I'll be ready."
entry.summary: Beau Greaves makes darts history by beating Daryl Gurney at the Czech Open to become the first woman to win a match on the European Tour.

It took them 10 minutes to score the first try as Saints failed to deal with Cook's kick, which fell for Leigh to spread the ball for Charnley to walk in on the right wing. He then celebrated by signing a mock contract and, moments later, the public address confirmed he had signed a new deal for the 2027 season. Leigh scored a second try four minutes later as Armstrong, Cook and Lachlan Lam combined from deep in their own half to break up the left before Armstrong sprinted in from halfway. Saints responded by working space for Douglas to go over in the right corner before phenomenal feet from Harry Robertson left the defence for dead and he sent Sailor under the posts. But Robertson then missed a tackle that allowed Innes Senior to break for Leigh and create Hanley's first try, before Ipape drove for the line, his offload went to ground but Cook grubbered in-goal and touched down. After half-time, St Helens blew a two-on-one on the left wing before they lost Percival - who recently announced he will retire at the end of the season - to the sin bin for a high tackle. Leigh eventually made the extra man count when a second set of six and a quick play-the-ball under the posts led to Ipape barging over. Shane Wright then gave a penalty away for obstruction in the shadow of his own posts and Leigh worked the ball to Hanley on the right, who burst through three tackles to find the line. Further tries in the rain would follow as Alick-Wiencke slid in before Mulhern charged over with the final play of the game. Leigh 'back on track' - reaction Leigh Leopards head coach Adrian Lam told BBC Radio Manchester: "We wanted to respond from last week and I'm pleased, it puts us back on track. "Josh [Charnley] is still playing as well as he has been, he's a fan favourite and a big part of this club. The legacy and DNA we've been building since we came back up - he's been a big part of that. "Had you had said to us a quarter of the way through [the season], would you accept where we are now? Absolutely." St Helens interim head coach Eamon O'Carroll told BBC Radio Merseyside: "The scoreline probably doesn't reflect the effort and I'm unbelievably proud of the players. "I've been in this role for six weeks and if there's one thing I wanted to get out of it, it is that we had a team that turned up for each other and we had that tonight. "It's great to give young lads a chance, ideally you'd like to do it with a few more senior players around them, so they're not exposed as much, but they can hold their heads up and they'll certainly be better for this experience." St Helens: Sailor; Douglas, Percival, Welsby, Cross; Robertson, Lomax; Klemmer, Humphreys, Horst, Keeley, Wright, Shorrocks. Interchanges: Marsh, Evans, Matagi, Knox.
entry.summary: Leigh Leopards secure a Super League top-six finish by thrashing St Helens, ending Saints' hopes of reaching the play-offs.

entry.title: Isak finally arrives as Gakpo proves value to Liverpool
entry.body: Isak finally arrives as Gakpo proves value to Liverpool - Published Alexander Isak was the Â£125m striker who finally arrived at Liverpool by tormenting Ipswich Town - while Cody Gakpo's virtuoso performance had them giving thanks he never left. The nuts and bolts of a comfortable Friday in Suffolk were that Liverpool won 2-0 - thanks to two Isak goals in the first nine minutes, giving them their first Premier League victory of the season and new manager Andoni Iraola's first since succeeding the sacked Arne Slot. Liverpool's win must be placed in the context of being against a newly promoted Ipswich Town who were game, but who shipped five goals at Manchester United last week and look ripe for the picking against attacking quality. The wider significance, however, was that Isak finally looked like the player Liverpool broke, at that time, the British transfer record to seal an acrimonious transfer from Newcastle United last summer. Throw in the added bonus that Bradley Barcola showed flashes of devastating pace in a 26-minute debut display after his Â£123m arrival from Paris St-Germain, and this was a night that ticked every box for Iraola and Liverpool. Even Barcola's bow, however, was overshadowed by Isak. The Sweden striker looked a lost soul in his first season at Liverpool, arriving out of condition after downing tools to secure his move from Tyneside, then troubled by injuries as he gave the impression of being the most expensive vanity purchase in British football history. He was outshone by fellow striker Hugo Ekitike, his statistics stark as he suffered along with many others in an astonishing decline amid Liverpool's dismal title defence that led to Slot's sacking only a year after he lifted the Premier League trophy. Isak played 22 games encompassing 1,033 minutes, scoring four goals at a rate of one every 258 minutes. He played 14 games in the Premier League totalling 703 minutes, scoring only three goals at a rate of one every 234 minutes. He has already equalled that league tally this season, but it was his demeanour as well as his lethal finishing that will have given Liverpool and Iraola confidence that the Isak code has finally been cracked. And it was done by utilising Isak at his best - running in behind defenders and pressing with pace. It was what made him such a hot property at Newcastle United, and made everything about his every miserable moment on the pitch with Liverpool last term such a mystery. It was also done in tandem with Gakpo, who could easily have been back in the north west preparing for Manchester City's game against Coventry City at Etihad Stadium had the move not collapsed. - Isak shines at last but Scherpen suffers - Ipswich v Liverpool player ratings - Published5 hours ago Gakpo was happy to join Enzo Maresca's Manchester City transition, but Liverpool's failure to sign Yankuba Minteh from Brighton or Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr meant he stayed at Anfield. And it might just be one of those twists of fate football can throw up as Gakpo delivered a masterclass of creation that meant this game was effectively over after nine minutes. Isak was the spearhead who delivered the defining moments, starting in the sixth minute when he took Gakpo's clever pass between Leif Davis and Jacob Greaves before thrashing a right-foot shot that carried too much power for Ipswich Town keeper Kjell Scherpen, although he had to do much, much better than divert the striker's effort into the net. The second, three minutes later, was stamped right through with class, bringing a beaming smile to the face of Iraola. Gakpo delivered a delicious pass with the outside of his right foot from inside his own half. Isak used a left-foot flick to move inside Greaves as Scherpen came out, before a touch with his right foot sent the Ipswich keeper the wrong way before rolling in a cool finish with his left. Perfection from Gakpo's start to Isak's finish. Isak had a desperately poor return to Tyneside on the opening day of the season, questions even coming about his performance after he scored in Liverpool's 2-2 draw at home to Nottingham Forest in their second game. This, however, was Isak played right - and playing right. Iraola said: "He's a massive player for us. My demands will probably not be about the goals. I know he is fit and in good shape. He's going to produce the numbers. "My fight with him will be more about other stuff, how to help the team in other situations - but it is good he has already played two full games, scoring the goals, so I am very happy to have him." And Isak added: "We were waiting for the first win. We talked about starting the game good, which we haven't done recently, so it was perfect for us to get two good quick goals. "With a normal pre-season, I think we are starting to get to the way we want to play. To be offensive and attack the defence. I think we did that. We scored two, and we could have scored more." Reflecting on his poor first season at Liverpool, Isak said: "It was not easy. It was obviously a long injury and a difficult season in general. I was thinking to have a good World Cup, and then to start off the season well, which I think I have done now. It's kind of behind me, but it wasn't easy." Portman Road is certainly a happy hunting ground for Isak. Since the start of the 2024-25 season, his five Premier League goals there are the joint most by any player at an away ground, equalling Erling Haaland's haul against Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park. Gakpo also struggled for his best form in the last campaign, but he has started this season in outstanding style. This was the elegant Netherlands forward at his best, not just by making two goals, but with his all-round performance. Liverpool captain and compatriot Virgil van Dijk is certainly delighted to still be lining up alongside his team-mate for club and country, saying: "It's massive. I said it before the transfer window had closed. "He's important for us, and he will be important this season. He showed it last week as well, and over the last couple of years. He needs to just keep going." The same challenge now applies to Isak. Iraola will not want this to be a false dawn for such an exceptional talent that had lost his way.
entry.summary: Has the real Alexander Isak finally arrived at Liverpool after his two-goal display in their Premier League win at Ipswich Town, asks chief football writer Phil McNulty?

entry.title: ‘Wheel of Fortune’ announcer Jim Thornton fired after pedophilia chat room incident - Los Angeles Times
entry.body: ‘Wheel of Fortune’ announcer Jim Thornton fired after pedophilia chat room incident - Click here to listen to this article - Share via See more from the L.A. Set us as preferred - “Wheel of Fortune” is cutting ties with its longtime announcer, Jim Thornton, following recent revelations that connected him to a disturbing chat room. - A representative for Sony Pictures Television says, “Jim Thornton’s employment with ‘Wheel of Fortune’ has been terminated, effective immediately.” “Wheel of Fortune” announcer Jim Thornton’s longtime tenure on the popular game show is officially over. A spokesperson for Sony Pictures Television, which produces “Wheel of Fortune,” confirmed in a statement shared with The Times on Friday that Thornton’s “employment with ‘Wheel of Fortune’ has been terminated, effective immediately,” following an investigation. Sony suspended Thornton on Tuesday amid an ongoing probe into then-unspecified allegations. A legal representative for Thornton, 61, did not immediately respond to The Times’ request for comment on Friday. A day before TMZ first reported on the announcer‘s firing, the outlet published numerous photos that show Thornton on his laptop aboard a flight visiting a website that describes itself as a support chat for “people who are attracted to children.” In photos taken by a neighboring passenger, Thornton’s computer screen appears to show messages of one user saying they “saw a couple of cute boys and a hot little girl” at a restaurant they referred to as an “All-you-can-eat Boyfett” and a second user referring to “CP,” commonly shorthand for child pornography. The photos published by TMZ also show Thornton, who is wearing a black jacket embroidered with the “Wheel of Fortune” logo on his sleeve, appearing to type into the chat room. New allegations emerge in the controversy surrounding longtime ‘Wheel of Fortune’ announcer Jim Thornton, who was suspended this week amid an ongoing probe by its production studio. Thornton’s attorney Allison Hart told TMZ that he became a suicide-prevention advocate after a loved one took their life two years ago and he has since spent time visiting crisis chat rooms to offer “support to individuals suffering from suicidal ideation.” According to TMZ, Thornton claimed an acquaintance from a suicide prevention group sent him a link to an unrelated, non-crisis chat room — the one seen in the photos. Thornton also reportedly said he quickly left the disturbing chat room “once he found out what it was.” Time stamps seen in the photos show Thornton remained in the chat room for nearly an hour. The passenger complained about Thornton to a flight attendant and shared the photos with the crew, according to TMZ. American Airlines informed the outlet that a passenger was met by law enforcement upon arrival at Los Angeles International Airport on May 14, although the airline did not identify the individual. Thornton’s attorney also told TMZ earlier this week that he “did not engage in any illegal conduct, was not arrested and has not been charged with any crime.” “When questioned about the complaint made by a fellow passenger on the flight, law enforcement spoke to him for five minutes or less, immediately determined that no wrongdoing had occurred and told my client he was free to go,” his attorney said. Thornton’s “Wheel of Fortune” tenure traces back to 2011 following the death of his predecessor, Charlie O’Donnell. His game show credits include “The Price Is Right,” “The Soup,” “Jeopardy!” and “Celebrity Wheel of Fortune.” He has performed voice work for the movie “Monsters, Inc.,” and video games including “Wall-E” and “Mafia II.” Times staff writer Andrea Flores contributed to this report.

entry.title: 'Spider-Noir' Canceled After One Season By Prime Video - Deadline
entry.body: Prime Video has opted not to proceed with a second season of the superhero series Spider-Noir starring Nicolas Cage. Spider-Noir was the second series ordered and first to make it to the screen under a multi-title deal between Amazon MGM Studios and Sony Pictures Television based on IP from Sony Pictures’ Universe of Marvel Characters. (The first, Spider-Man spinoff Silk, was ultimately scrapped.) Amazon was expected to wait and see how Spider-Noir does before making a decision on other shows. While the Nicolas Cage vehicle will not be continuing, the Amazon-Sony TV collaboration it was part of will. The two sides are carrying on with development of multiple projects, with one of them said to be nearing a series order. Its concept is being kept under wraps. All shows under the deal have a linear debut on Amazon’s MGM+ platform followed by a streaming release on sibling Prime Video. Spider-Noir fared well with both reviewers and viewers, earning a 92% critics score and 90% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes and landing 11 Emmy Award nominations — the most of any Prime Video series in 2026. Watch on Deadline RELATED: 2026 TV Series Renewals Photo Gallery The pull of recognizable IP and Oscar winner Cage in his first TV role helped Spider-Noir to a solid launch at No.2 on Nielsen’s U.S Top 10 for original series for its first week, bringing in 851 million minutes viewed. (The show premiered May 25 on MGM+ and May 27 globally on Prime Video.) Over its first six weeks, the comedy-drama generated 2.6 billion viewing minutes in the U.S., according to Nielsen Streaming Content Ratings. But Spider-Noir didn’t have the staying power of other Prime Video recent releases such as Off Campus, Reacher and Ride Or Die, dropping off the platform’s daily Top 10 rankings relatively quickly. The respectable but not outsized viewership was coupled with the high cost for the lavish production, which filmed both color and black & white versions. Since streamers base their renewal decisions primarily on cost vs. performance, the ratio likely factored into the call not to continue Spider-Noir. RELATED: Emmy Nominations 2026: The Complete List On the bright side, Season 1 told largely a complete story with just a few loose threads left, so fans will not be left hanging too much by the cancellation. Based on the Marvel comic Spider-Man Noir, the live-action Spider-Noir follows Ben Reilly (Nicolas Cage), a seasoned, down-on-his-luck private investigator in 1930s New York, who is forced to grapple with his past life following a deeply personal tragedy, as the city’s one and only superhero. Led by Cage, the cast also included Lamorne Morris, Li Jun Li, Karen Rodriguez, Abraham Popoola, Jack Huston and Brendan Gleeson. Oren Uziel and Steve Lightfoot served as co-showrunners and executive producers. The two developed the series with the team behind Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse: Phil Lord, Christopher Miller, and Amy Pascal. Lord and Miller executive produced Spider-Noir for their Lord Miller banner, along with Aditya Sood and Dan Shear. Pascal also served as an executive producer via Pascal Pictures, as did Cage and Pavlina Hatoupis. Harry Bradbeer directed and executive produced the first two episodes. entry.title: Lauryn Hill, Wyclef and Giggs among surprise guests at Jay-Z's long-awaited UK show
entry.body: Lauryn Hill, Wyclef and Giggs among surprise guests at Jay-Z's long-awaited UK show - Published Jay-Z's first headline solo show in the UK in more than a decade saw him celebrate hip-hop culture alongside a host of special guests, including Lauryn Hill, Wyclef Jean and Giggs. The US rap superstar rolled back the years for more than two hours - playing hits like 99 Problems, Empire State of Mind and Dead Presidents - as he took to the stage at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Friday night for the first of two shows in London this weekend. The run is part of his Jay-Z 30 tour, which is marking the 30th anniversary of his debut album, Reasonable Doubt, and his culture-shaping career that followed. Fans of his wife BeyoncÃ© had hoped she would join him on stage, like she did at two of his three New York shows this summer, as she was also celebrating her 45th birthday on Friday. Toward the end of the show, Jay-Z mentioned it was a "young lady's birthday", sending the crowd into a frenzy, but he joked that he couldn't make her perform on her big day. Instead he asked the crowd to join him in singing Happy Birthday to the US superstar, who was sat in a private box, while sparkler-like fireworks erupted in the sky. BeyoncÃ© serenaded on her birthday The show's opening set the tone for the star-studded evening to follow, as British actor Sir Idris Elba kicked things off by performing the intro track to his 2007 album, American Gangster. As Jay-Z took to the stage, he recalled coming to London in 1989 with his mentor Jaz-O and seeing "what was possible" and it became a "special" place in his career. His return to the capital this time round was explosive, with the rapper rattling through a string of hits like Izzo (H.O.V.A.), On To The Next One and Song Cry. Throughout the show, vintage video clips and moments from his early career played across a massive LED screen, while an orchestra and a few guitarists accompanied him on stage. There was no sign of Rihanna or Alicia Keys, who both made appearances during the New York run for their collaboration tracks, but the crowd made up for their absence by chanting back their lyrics during Run This Town and Empire State of Mind. Jay-Z also took a moment to thank his fans who have been there from the beginning, telling them that "music saved my life". His reflective mood continued as he performed Hard Knock Life (Ghetto Anthem) and Where I'm From, which explores his upbringing in the Marcy housing projects in Brooklyn, New York. He cranked the energy back up for his 2011 hit No Church in the Wild, which was amplified by firey pyrotechnics that radiated heat through the stadium. Originally a collaboration with controversial rapper Ye, also known as Kanye West, Jay-Z left his voice in for the chorus but cut his verses out. US DJ Khaled had a brief moment on stage while Jay-Z changed, but it was the appearance of London-born rapper Giggs which got the crowd erupting. He appeared overwhelmed at one stage, his hand clutching his face, as he took in the packed crowd while performing his track Talkin Da Hardest alongside Jay-Z. The surprise guests didn't stop there, as Lauryn Hill and Wyclef Jean from the 90s American hip-hop collective Fugees reunited to perform their hit tracks Ready or Not, Killing Me Softly With His Song and Fu-Gee-La. It was a full circle moment for both them and Jay-Z as he recalled supporting them on their European tour. The US rap superstar closed out the night with rousing renditions of Public Service Announcement (Interlude) and Numb/Encore, hailing it as a "legendary night" that he would "never forget". The crowd appeared to agree as thousands praised him by holding up his famous diamond hand gesture. Fans had travelled from across the UK and the world to see the rapper, including Prince Dean Sithole, who hailed Jay-Z as one of his role models. "I think he's very impacting, especially for us black people because we don't get a lot of recognition," the 19-year-old from Leeds told BBC Newsbeat. "Seeing him today shows that dreams are possible and you can be that person that you want to be." Jay-Z, real name Shawn Carter, broke through with his 1996 debut album, but it was his third record, Vol. 2: Hard Knock Life, in 1998 which landed him the top spot in the US charts for the first time and a best rap album Grammy. He went on to establish himself as one of the most influential figures in hip-hop, releasing 13 solo studio albums and several collaboration records, which have secured him 25 Grammy Awards. He was also the first rapper inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2017, as well being inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2021. Over the years, he has also become one of the most prominent music mogul's in the world, with his company Roc Nation representing a host of top talent and, in recent years, it has been behind the Super Bowl half-time show. In 2019, he was declared hip-hop's first billionaire by Forbes, having built an empire based on music, property, fashion and investments alongside his wife BeyoncÃ©. The power couple have three children, daughter Blue Ivy, 14, and 9-year-old twins, Rumi and Sir. - Published23 February 2017 - Published3 June 2019 - Published23 October 2023
entry.summary: The US rapper rolled back the years for more than two hours at the first of his two shows in London.

entry.title: Dolly Parton’s Sister Stella Speaks Out Against ‘AI and Endless Garbage’ Posted Online After Icon’s Death
entry.body: Dolly Parton’s Sister Stella Speaks Out Against ‘AI and Endless Garbage’ Posted Online After Icon’s Death Dolly Parton’s sister Stella is asking people to “show more compassion” as her family grieves the loss and called out the wave of fake AI content posted online following Parton’s death. Stella began her message by thanking those who showed “genuine” support toward her family during this difficult time. “We will be okay in time but each of us will grieve in our own personal way,” Stella continued. “Sadly, because of the way our lives have been in front of the public, we have no choice but to be subjected to incredible pressure and insensitivity from strangers.” Stella addressed the “tremendous amount of AI and endless garbage being posted everyday” since Dolly’s death and said “it’s been challenging to absorb and or ignore. ” She said the country legend “loved her fans and the public in general,” adding, “That is the reason she chose not to express her opinions on a lot of things like politics, religion and individuals in the public eye. She knew as well as anyone what a negative vortex that could turn into which is nothing but a huge waste of positive energy.” She urged the public to also use her sister’s life “as an example for tolerance and respect toward others.” She added, “It’s not about the most clever comments, fake AI garbage or snarky tweets. At the end of the day or the end of a life, how will you feel about yourself? It’s not about what other individuals you will never meet think of you!” Following Parton’s death on Aug. 25 at 80, Stella praised her sister’s generosity and kindness in a heartfelt remembrance. In her tribute, Stella wrote, “My sister was always thinking of others and if you want to honor her legacy, show more kindness, lift others up, and give more of your time and resources, as she continued to do to the very end.”
entry.summary: Stella Parton urged people to "show more compassion and wisdom" moving forward

entry.title: Bruce Campbell has 5 years to live, he says during podcast appearance - The Detroit News
entry.body: Bruce Campbell has 5 years to live, he says during podcast appearance The Royal Oak-born actor and 'Evil Dead' star announced his cancer diagnosis earlier this year. Royal Oak-born actor and cult movie icon Bruce Campbell said during an appearance on "The Adam Carolla Show" this week that he has five years to live. Campbell announced in March that he has been diagnosed with a "treatable" but not "curable" form of cancer. He has not disclosed the type of cancer with which he has been diagnosed. "The current thing is a five-year deal," Campbell told Carolla during the episode, which was posted Sept. "So the prognosis is you have five years to live?" Carolla asked Campbell. "Give or take," Campbell said. The episode is posted below; the cancer discussion begins around the 11:30 mark. "I've decided, pretty specifically, to live with it, not die from it," the "Evil Dead" actor said of his diagnosis. "You can go down a massive rabbit hole. The cancer rabbit hole is enormous. You can go into focus groups of 10,000 guys who have what you have. I wouldn't touch it with a 10-foot pole. "It's a whack-a-mole life, literally," Campbell said of living with cancer. "Cancer compromises s--- inside your body. So then you go, 'deal with that,' so then you deal with that. And then you sort of wait for it to then compromise something else. Meanwhile, you're trying to put out the whole fire." Campbell, 68, was on Carolla's show to talk about his latest movie, "Ernie & Emma," which he brought to Detroit's Redford Theatre in June. It's a dramedy about a man who takes a road trip with his wife's ashes following her death. He's bringing the film on an 18-date tour of Alamo Drafthouse locations that kicks off Sept. 4 in Los Angeles and wraps up Nov. Campbell told The Detroit News in May that he's doing his best to stay steady amid his health diagnosis. "That's the word I'm gonna use. I'm managing my situation, and I'm gonna live my life as close to what is normal as I can for as long as I can. It's just that simple." agraham@detroitnews.com

entry.title: Beyoncé’s ‘B’Day’ Reissue Samples Selena and Celia Cruz, But It’s Not Her First Latin Tribute
entry.body: Beyoncé’s ‘B’Day’ Reissue Samples Selena and Celia Cruz, But It’s Not Her First Latin Tribute Beyoncé just released the 20th anniversary edition of her 2006 classic B’Day with a definitive Latin music twist. Bey sings in Spanish for a handful of songs, uses samples from icons like Celia Cruz and Selena Quintanilla, and even taps Maluma for a brand new track. It’s an exciting display, but it’s not her first rodeo with Latin music. On new track “Irreemplazable (Como La Flor),” Beyoncé interpolates Selena Quintanilla’s 1992 hit “Como La Flor,” which took the music world by surprise. But the move has been a long time coming for Queen Bey. As a Houston native, the superstar used to listen to Selena on the radio. On new track “Irreemplazable (Como La Flor),” Beyoncé interpolates Selena Quintanilla’s 1992 hit “Como La Flor,” which took the music world by surprise. But the move has been a long time coming for Queen Bey. As a Houston native, the superstar used to listen to Selena on the radio. Speaking to MTV Tr3s years ago, she recalled actually meeting Selena in Texas. “I did actually meet Selena in The Galleria mall in Houston, but I didn’t say much to Selena because I wasn’t a celebrity and I just saw her and said, ‘Hello’ and kept it moving,” she recalled back then. “Definitely growing up in Texas, I heard her on the radio and I think listening to her album, even though I didn’t know exactly what she was singing, it helped me in the studio with my pronunciation.” The Irreemplazable EP from 2007 was actually Beyoncé’s first full foray into Latin music. The project featured eight tracks that were mostly recorded in Spanish with the help of Rudy Pérez, a Grammy-winning producer behind some of the biggest ballads in Latin music. The superstar also tapped Mexican icon Alejandro Fernández for “Amor Gitano” and Puerto Rican rapper Voltio for the Timbaland remix of “Get Me Bodied.” The Selena influence is loud and clear on the norteña remix of “Irreemplazable.” Most notably, the EP features “Beautiful Liar,” Beyoncé’s pivotal collaboration with Shakira. Beyoncé’s work with Latin music, and Colombian musicians specifically, didn’t stop there. In 2017, she hopped on J Balvin’s “Mi Gente” and helped turned it into a hit that defined Latin pop’s power in the mid-2010s. The following year, Queen Bey even invited Balvin to perform the track with her at her historic Coachella headlining set. “It was a life-changing thing for culture in general,” Balvin told Rolling Stone earlier this year. “Those moments that mark a before and after in our game of urban or Latin music in general. That really was a step up.” Beyoncé continues to show her love for Colombians with the B’Day reissue by releasing new song alongside Colombian hitmaker Maluma, who could barely believe the achievement himself. The singer took to social media to film his reaction to the song’s release. “Marica, I never thought I would say this. Be ready for what I’m about to say. ‘Get You Bodied (Tumbao)’ featuring Beyonce is out now. Colombia in the house, que chimba,” Maluma said on his Instagram stories. “Cuerpo (Tumbao)” is one of Beyoncé’s most Latin-inspired tracks to date, and was even co-written and co-produced by Édgar Barrera, a go-to voice in Latin music right now. Celia Cruz’s presence is also all over the record, first with a sample from her 2001 song “La Negra Tiene Tumbao” and later with a lyrical reference to the salsa icon’s acceptance speech at the 2002 Latin Grammys. “Excuse my English is not very good looking,” Cruz said while accepting the award for Best Salsa Album for La Negra Tiene Tumbao. In “Cuerpo (Tumbao),” Beyoncé says, “My Spanish is not very good looking.” Much like with Selena, Cruz has been influencing Beyoncé’s music for years. “Beyoncé has long admired Cruz’s pride in her African culture; her refusal to bend in the wake of racism, colorism and the narrow definition of beauty,” reads a press release. “In a time when society wanted her to be bitter and broken down, she boldly claimed her Blackness. The sample was the perfect fit for a song that pushes strength and confidence on the dancefloor and in life.”
entry.summary: Queen Bey's newest project honors major Latin stars — and calls back to her history with Latin music

entry.title: ‘A Long Winter’ Review: Andrew Haigh’s Moody Drama, Set on a Farm in the Rockies in the Early ’50s, Is a Sweeping Act of Cinematic Storytelling
entry.body: One definition of great cinematography is pretty pictures that move. On that score, “A Long Winter,” the majestically moody new drama written and directed by Andrew Haigh (“All of Us Strangers”), more than qualifies. It’s set on a remote farm nestled high in the Rocky Mountains in the early 1950s, and the images — of jutting peaks and plunging valleys, of endless stretches of pine, of the craggy frosted grandeur of it all — are vivid enough to carry you away. Yet the real definition of great cinematography is when a filmmaker, working with a bold camera artist (in this case, André Turpin), frames the images so they don’t just dazzle but lure the audience, unfolding the action with a shimmering inquiry and suspense, as if each shot were another sentence in the story it’s telling. That’s the way “A Long Winter” works. Based on a novella by Colm Tóibín, it’s a film austere enough to risk alienating its audience, yet once you get onto its wavelength you stay right there, inside the movie’s world. For a while, “A Long Winter” is so authentically homespun that you may feel primed for a kind of art-house Laura Ingalls Wilder experience. In a stately, creaky mountainside farmhouse, Mikey (Fred Hechinger) and Tom (Kit Connor) are adult brothers who sleep in beds right next to each other. They have a caring and respectful relationship that feels pre-media enough to seem downright exotic. But Tom is impatient with their sedentary lives, raising chickens and rabbits (which they sell for their pelts). He’s about to leave for Army service in Korea. Mikey, by contrast, says he loves this life — the tranquility of it, which he finds comforting. He left for a while too (to go to Idaho), but ultimately came back. As the two have dinner with their parents, the taciturn Lester (Ebon Moss-Bachrach) and the radiant Louise (Caitríona Balfe), the movie shows us what it’s like to feel protected by an old-world American family coziness. Popular on Variety It’s soon apparent, though, that there are dark clouds adrift in this clan. Loise, vibrant but tense, gets through her days by drinking wine. She tries to hide the extent of it, but Mikey — the last one in the family to know — has now figured it out. Early on, he and his folks pile into their ancient wood-sided Ford station wagon, riding down the mountain to the small town nearby, in order to purchase supplies. The town looks depressed (there’s a condemned movie theater that still has “The Snake Pit,” from 1948, on its marquee), but there’s a life to it, and Mike observes his mother having an afternoon drink and then lying about it. It’s the deception, of course, that’s the red flag. Lester has always known about her drinking, but the moment has come (not the first) when he decides to intervene. Back home, after a heating-oil delivery (which is also a wine delivery), he throws out all of Louise’s cheap rotgut wine. He has decided, with a puritanical insistence, that he’s going to heal her by making her quit the booze cold turkey. But she’s having none of that; she feels like she needs the drink to survive. Caitríona Balfe acts with the impacted fervor of someone who’s caught in a life she chose but no longer wants. And so, without her crutch, she leaves — just like that. As the first winter storm is coming. Is she seeking alcohol or death? With Louise suddenly out of the picture, we may think that the movie has lost its most interesting character. “A Long Winter,” set over the following three snowbound months, turns into a family drama of morose and foreboding mystery. Mikey adores his mother, problematic though she is. His father, on the other hand, is a piece of work. Ebon Moss-Bachrach seems to have been put on earth to play men who are total pills, and here he gives us the scowling, mustached, man-of-few-words frontier version. Lester and Mikey, engaging the local police, along with some relatives, begin the process of searching for Louise, but she has vanished with such eerie completeness that for a while I thought “A Long Winter” might turn out to be a ghost story — one that starts with an hour of realistic exposition. There’s nothing supernatural about the movie. In a way, though, it is a ghost story. Louise — the presence of her absence — hovers over the wintry landscapes like a figment of loss and guilt. Her story, we realize, is tragic, but part of what makes it wounding is that the movie doesn’t demonize. Moss-Bachrach’s Lester, who originally came from New York City, is a stern taskmaster who wanted to be a farmer and wooed Louise over from the other side of the mountain; he thought the life they’d lead would be magical. But she grew disenchanted with it; she began to yearn for the middle-class life she saw in her Cosmopolitan magazines. And he couldn’t handle the disappointment of her unhappiness. The movie fills in the backstory of this slow-motion trauma in a way that feels wrenchingly lifelike. Only it’s Mikey who now bears the burden of it. “A Long Winter” is somber and placid yet told with such quiet confidence that it gets its hooks in you. The film is really about how Mikey discovers his inner life. An early scene, in which he makes eye contact with a young cop in town, is the tip-off — that Mikey is attracted to men. And what’s dramatic about this is that having grown up on a remote mountain farm in the 1940s, away from almost any remnant of civilization, Mikey has zero context for his erotic yearnings. He’s not even spooked by them (as we might expect him to be). Instead, Andrew Haigh, who has made such potent dramas of queer life (starting with “Weekend”), uses this story to craft the rare portrait of gay consciousness that feels rooted in an Edenic innocence. As Mikey, Fred Hechinger gives off young Tobey Maguire vibes, and the movie uses that aura with compelling poignance. Louise, in all her flaws, was Mikey’s link to love. Now his link to love is that young officer, and the pictures he sees in his mother’s magazines, and the young man who comes to live with them as a cook and housekeeper — Jimmy (D’Pharaoh Woon-A-Tai), a biracial Native American, who is stoic and solemn enough to suggest a Kenneth Anger fever dream. You could say that there’s a “Brokeback” feeling to it all, with homoeroticism suffusing a period piece set before those feelings had been allowed into the culture. But “Brokeback Mountain” was a fully realized love story. “A Long Winter” is never consummated in that way. As the winter fades, and the vultures come, the movie points to something else: how a mother’s end could be the bridge to her son’s beginning.

entry.title: Trump envoys Witkoff and Kushner to travel to Moscow and Kyiv this weekend
entry.body: President Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will travel this weekend to Moscow and Kyiv for talks on ending the war, U.S. officials said. Why it matters: This will be the first visit by Witkoff and Kushner to Kyiv since President Trump returned to office. State of play: Witkoff and Kushner will travel on Friday, hold talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin on Saturday and then meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv on Sunday. The visit by Trump's envoys comes 10 days after CIA Director John Ratcliffe met with the heads of the Russian intelligence and security services in Moscow. Ratcliffe was trying to learn whether the Russian intelligence chiefs could persuade Putin to pursue diplomacy with the goal of ending the war. Witkoff and Kushner met with President Trump at the White House Thursday to discuss the trip. Between the lines: Ukrainian and U.S. officials said they've been discussing the Kyiv trip for months. In recent days, they said, the trip was on and off several times for different reasons before they settled on this weekend. Catch up quick: Negotiations between Russia and Ukraine mediated by the Trump administration were paused in mid-February after the Iran war started. Witkoff and Kushner have held separate talks over the past few months with Russian and Ukrainian negotiators, but little progress has been made. Zelensky's chief of staff, Kyrylo Budanov, told local media last week that U.S.-mediated talks with Russia could resume in September. Yes, but: Ukrainian officials are highly skeptical of Putin's intentions and say they have intelligence that suggests Putin is planning a major escalation of the war. Russia has also intensified missile and drone strikes on Ukrainian cities, including Kyiv. Zelensky's deputy chief of staff, Pavlo Palisa, told reporters on Friday that Putin has ordered his military to prepare several operational scenarios for an offensive in northern Ukraine, with Kyiv and Chernihiv identified as key areas. Putin has also rejected several proposals by the Trump administration to hold a trilateral summit with Trump and Zelensky to try to reach a diplomatic breakthrough. What they're saying: Zelensky confirmed the meetings on X and said he expects the one in Kyiv to take place in the coming days. "This is very important," he wrote. "It is important that America remain actively engaged. We are ready to meet with them in Ukraine — properly and substantively."

entry.title: Trump brushes off accusations of Russian sabotage against NATO allies
entry.body: President Donald Trump dodged a chance Friday to condemn President Vladimir Putin over allegations that Russia has conducted espionage attacks on NATO nations. Trump, speaking to reporters at the White House, brushed off a question about one such apparent incident — the discovery of explosive-laden drones Aug. 4 at the Leipzig airport in Germany that officials have linked to Russia. “I speak to him,” Trump said of the Russian leader. “I know him very well. Putin is not looking to attack NATO territory." Trump did not elaborate further on the attack or why he would be so quick to dismiss an apparent attack on a fellow member of NATO, an alliance rooted in the concept of a shared defense against Moscow. The discovery of the drones packed with explosives, including one alongside a Ukrainian jet and another at a NATO logistics hub, appear to be what European security officials have characterized as a form of hybrid warfare by Russia against nations that have supported Ukraine since Putin launched a full-scale invasion there in 2022. German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius is set to meet with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in Washington later this month, when the two men will likely discuss the attack. NATO’s Secretary-General Mark Rutte has thrown his support behind Germany and said he welcomed its retaliatory measures for the Russian attacks. Tensions between Russia and the 32-member alliance, which was created in 1949 to address threats by the Soviet Union, have grown amid plots targeting European defenses and Russia’s ongoing war in Ukraine. Trump’s reaction to the question about the drones comes as NATO members have questioned whether they can rely on the U.S. to come to their aid in times of need. A POLITICO poll showed that trust in the U.S. among four key NATO allies had dropped sharply over the past year amid disputes with Washington and calls from the Trump administration to spend more on their own defense . Trump, who has long expressed admiration for Putin, has repeatedly threatened to leave the alliance, accusing NATO for failing to help with the Iran war.
